subject: Payment authorization failed for GreenByte - next steps
messages:
From: Amelia Rivera <amelia@greenbyte.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement <procurement@greenbyte.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: Failed payment attempt on invoice GB-247

Hi Jonas,

We got an email from Stripe this morning saying the payment for invoice GB-247 (Dec usage) failed to authorize. The notification shows 'card_declined - do_not_honor' and the customer email on the invoice is finance@greenbyte.ai. Invoice PDF attached. Can you advise the quickest way to get this retried? Our procurement team is on a freeze until EOD so we may need a one-off manual retry or an invoice reissue with updated billing terms.

Attached: auth-failure-screenshot.png, greenbyte-invoice-GB-247.pdf

Thanks,
Amelia Rivera
Head of Operations
GreenByte Analytics
amelia@greenbyte.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Rivera <amelia@greenbyte.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Failed payment attempt on invoice GB-247

Hi Amelia — thanks for the heads up and for attaching the screenshots. Quick answers up front:

- We can attempt a one-time manual retry from our billing console (requires authorization from your finance contact).
- Alternatively, we can create a short-term invoice with a net-14 window and send a new payment link.
- If the card is being rejected by the issuing bank (do_not_honor), retries rarely succeed unless the customer updates the card or the bank lifts a hold.

Next steps I propose:
1) If finance can confirm authorization, reply-all with the OK and we will queue a manual retry (no additional fee).
2) If procurement prefers an updated invoice, tell us the new payment term and we will issue a replacement invoice and resend the link.
3) If there's a suspected fraud/3DS issue, we can route the transaction to a lower-failure path (different Stripe relay) — Marissa, can you outline the operational steps for that?

Marissa / Michael — please include the HubSpot deal link in the reply and the expected retry window (I put 24-48h). We need to document any manual retries for audit.

Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Failed payment attempt on invoice GB-247

Thanks Amelia / Jonas — looping in Billing Ops (Michael) and adding a couple concrete options so procurement can decide quickly.

Option A — Manual retry (fastest)
- We will attempt a single manual retry through Stripe within 24 hours.
- Requires explicit written approval from the finance email on file (finance@greenbyte.ai).
- We'll capture POS metadata and attach the attempt to the invoice for audit.

Option B — Reissue invoice
- We can cancel GB-247 and issue GB-247-R1 with net-14 and a new payment link (no change to amounts).
- This avoids any bank retry rules that are denying auth attempts.

Option C — Card update flow
- Send a secure hosted card update link to the finance user (best for long-term).
- We can configure the link to expire in 72 hours and notify you the moment a new card is added.

Michael: if you advise the accounting log entry wording so GreenByte's AP team can reconcile (reference: GB-247 / original stripe txn id), I'll add it to the HubSpot record.

Also cc'ing procurement contact in case they want the reissue route. If procurement confirms 'manual retry', we will start it and follow up with a success/failure status.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Billing Ops, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Hi Marissa / Jonas,

Thanks for the clear options. Procurement won’t authorize a retry until they confirm the cardholder will approve — they asked us to reissue the invoice with net-14 and resend the link so they can process it in their weekly run. Please issue GB-247-R1 and send the hosted payment link to finance@greenbyte.ai.

Also: the finance team noticed an earlier authorization that was labeled 'suspected_fraud' in mid-December — they are going to check with their bank but don’t want a second payment hit on the same card. If possible, please mark this as 'reissued' in the invoice memo and include the original Stripe txn id so their AP team can reconcile.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — can you confirm when the new invoice will be sent?

Best,
Amelia Rivera
Head of Operations
GreenByte Analytics
